environment.description: Same Ktor microservice in EKS pod (namespace: audit-system) with identical IAM role. S3 traffic is routed exclusively through a com.amazonaws.us-east-1.s3 Gateway VPC Endpoint (vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890). The VPC endpoint has a resource policy with a condition block requiring that all PutObject requests include a specific content-type constraint AND that the object key must match a prefix pattern validated by StringLike on s3:prefix. Additionally, the endpoint policy includes a condition aws:ResourceTag/log-integrity=verified which is only present on objects written by the Lambda-based log sanitizer (not directly by the service). The effective endpoint policy denies any PutObject where the request body size exceeds 2048 bytes OR where the Content-Type is not exactly 'application/json; charset=utf-8' (note: the code sends 'application/json' without charset, meaning all direct writes from this service are DENIED by the endpoint policy). The pod has no alternative network path to S3 due to security group egress rules restricting 443 traffic to the VPC endpoint prefix list only (pl-63a5400a).

config.log_pipeline: CloudWatch Logs agent -> Splunk HEC (raw ingestion)
config.note: Service writes Content-Type 'application/json' (without charset) so all PutObject calls are denied by endpoint policy. Audit logs only reach S3 via a separate Lambda sanitizer that re-encodes and validates JSON structure before writing with correct Content-Type.
